title: Defining a Relativity-Proof Notion of the Present via Spatio-temporal Indeterminism
version: Foundations of Physics 50 (2020), 644–664; published online 2019-06-14; open-access version of record
relevance: Definitions 6–12 and Theorem 1 provide the exact abstract BST hypothesis class and co-presentness definitions checked against the dense-comb candidate.
locators: Definitions 6–12, pp. 657–660; Fact 4, p. 660; Theorem 1 and footnote 26, pp. 661–662; footnote 23, p. 657
assumptions: BST structure as defined in Definition 6: dense endpoint-free partial order; lower-bounded chains have infima in W; upper-bounded chains have history-relative suprema; chain prior-choice principle. Definition 6 expressly omits Weiner's postulate in footnote 23.
conclusion: The stated Theorem 1 says every history of every non-featureless BST structure has co-presentness neither identity nor universal. Direct audit finds the dense-comb order refutes the identity exclusion on its trunk history.
proof_status: Theorem 1 is stated without a proof immediately following it; this source record reports an independent countermodel audit, not a source proof audit.
limits: An abstract BST counterexample alone establishes no result about Minkowski embeddings, physically realized relativistic manifolds, presentism, or objective passage.
open_questions: Priority and any applicable additional physical/manifold restrictions are not settled by this review.
